In Chamber
 Hon'Ble Siddharth, J. 
1. Despite service of notice on respondent no.2, no one has turned up to oppose this revision.

2. Heard Sri Raghuvansh Chandra, learned counsel for revisionist; learned Aga for State and
perused the trial court record.

3.  This criminal revision has been filed against the judgment and order dated 23.01.2024, passed by Children's Court, Meerut, in Criminal Appeal No. 164 of 2023, dismissing the appeal, confirming the order dated 05.10.2023, passed by Juvenile Justice Board, Meerut, in Case No. 45 of 2023,
dismissing the application to declare revisionist juvenile, arising out of case crime no. 71/2022,
under sections- 452, 376(3), 302 of I.P.C., and section 3/4(2) of POCSO Act, Police Station- Falavada, District- Meerut.
4.

The brief facts of the case are that on 25.11.2022 an application was filed by the revisionist to declare him juvenile on the basis of the High School Certificate wherein his date of birth is recorded as 14.06.2006.

By the order dated 21.03.2023, the Board assessed the age of revisionist as 15 years,
10 months and 17 days on the basis of High School Certificate and declared him juvenile.

5. Against the order dated 21.03.2025 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, the informant filed an Appeal and the Appellate Court by its order dated 25.07.2023 remanded the mater to the Board for reassessing the educational certificates of the revisionist and determine his age on the date of incident accordingly.

6. The Juvenile Justice Board vide order dated 05.10.2023 only directed ossification test of the revisionist and on the basis of the same declared him to be adult aged more than 18 years at the time of incident and the appellate court has affirmed the same.

The Learned Counsel for the revisionist submits that the Juvenile Justice Board did not complied the order of the appellate court dated 25.07.2023 passed earlier for reconsideration of educational documents of the revisionist and passed illegal order however the appellate court instead of setting aside the same has affirmed the same illegally.

7. This Court after considering the rival submissions finds that although the Juvenile Justice Board did not complied the directions of the appellate court earlier but the appellate court has reconsidered the material on record and has found that as per Section-94(2)(i) of the Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act, 2015 the matriculation certificate or equivalent certificate has been given first priority which was produced by the revisionist before the Board in support of his claim of juvenility.

sentences.text: 2 revisionist is his eldest son born on 14.06.2006.
He has studied from 1 to class-5th in a private school in the village which has now closed.
He does not remembers the name of the school.
He informed the age of the revisionist in School on the basis of his memory and did not provided any date of birth certificate to the School.

8. A.W.-2, Head Mistress of the School, stated that revisionist was admitted in her School in Class-VIIIth on 02.04.2018 which he passed on 30.03.2019 his date of birth recorded in S.R.
Register was 14.06.2006.
Transfer Certificate of Class-VIII was issued in favour of the father of the revisionist.

The appellate court found that the date of birth mentioned in the Transfer Certificate of Class-VIIIth of the revisionist was not based on any credible evidence, therefore, the underlying document of the High School Certificate was not reliable and in view of the Judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sanjeev Kumar Gupta Vs. State of U.P. & Others, reported in AIR 2019 (SC)
4364, this High School Certificate was not reliable for the purpose of his age determination.

sentences.text: Even as per ossification test report he was found to be adult.

9. In the case of Bhagwan Jagannath Markad Vs. State of Maharashtra ( 2016) 10 SCC 537, it is held that the power of an appellate court are as wide as the trial court and the appellate court can review whole evidence and all relevant circumstances to arrive at its own conclusion.

entities.text: Bhagwan Jagannath Markad Vs. State of Maharashtra ( 2016) 10 SCC 537
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. The counsel for the revisionist has placed reliance on the Judgment of the Apex Court in the Case of Rishipal Singh Solanki Vs. State of U.P. (2022) 8 SCC 602, passed in Criminal Appeal No.1240 of 2021 and has submitted that where there was no contrary evidence produced against the age of accused mentioned in the matriculation certificate and accused was found to be juvenile as per the medical test he was required to be declared juvenile.

entities.text: Rishipal Singh Solanki Vs. State of U.P. (2022) 8 SCC 602
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This court finds that in this case the revisionist failed to prove that his High School Certificate was based on reliable underlying documents.

Further the ossification test report of the revisionist was against him, therefore, the benefit of the Judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Rishipal Singh Solanki (supra) can not be extended to the revisionist.
11. The Judgments and Orders passed by both the Courts below are in accordance with law and do not call for any interference by this Court.
12. This revision is accordingly dismissed.
